articles.title: US Air Force outlines the fighter fleet it needs by 2035
articles.summary: A new Air Force report calls for 1,509 combat-coded fighters by 2035, with F-35s making up 40% of the fleet and F-47s replacing F-22s.

articles.title: Commander of Air Combat Command tours Luke AFB
articles.summary: U.S. Air Force Gen. Adrian Spain, commander of Air Combat Command, recently visited Luke Air Force Base to engage with Airmen and observe how the 56th Fighter Wing develops combat-ready Airmen and fighter pilots.

articles.title: Pentagon AI oversight office struggles to keep pace with department’s ambitions, GAO finds
articles.summary: The Pentagon office tapped in 2022 to oversee the military’s responsible use of AI had filled just three of 10 authorized positions as of February 2026.

articles.title: Road to NTC: Light support battalion moves mountains (and Humvees)
articles.summary: Soldiers assigned to the Washington Army National Guard's 181st Light Support Battalion conducted a two-day deployment readiness exercise at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, Oct. 15–16, 2026, as part of preparations for an upcoming National Training Center rotation at Fort Irwin, California.

articles.title: Critical Industrial Base Facility Breaks Ground Thanks to Australian Submarine Industrial Base Contribution
articles.summary: U.S. Navy leaders joined industry partners, members of the Jackson County Economic Development Foundation, Inc., and representatives from the Australian Embassy to break ground on a new facility in Pascagoula, Miss., that will manufacture critical components for in-service and new-construction submarines.

articles.title: Got milk? US Army refines its pasteurization power
articles.summary: Thirteen U.S. Army Veterinary Corps officers milked a trip to Denmark last month, completing Europe Dairy Pasteurization Audit Training.

articles.title: ILLINOIS ARMY NATIONAL GUARD OFFICER PROMOTED TO MAJOR
articles.summary: Capt. Thaddaeus Carr was promoted to major during a ceremony on Oct. 18 at Cantigny Park in Wheaton, Illinois, recognizing his military service, professional development and contributions to military intelligence.
